holidays.name: National Cranberry Relish Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the tart, tangy side dish that shows up on Thanksgiving tables, whether it's chunky homemade relish or the can-shaped jelly that slides out with ridges intact.
holidays.origin: Part of the unofficial food-holiday calendar, placed just before Thanksgiving in the US. Cranberries are one of the few major fruits native to North America, and Indigenous peoples used them as food, dye, and medicine long before the holiday existed.
holidays.funFact: Cranberries bounce when ripe, which is why growers historically tested them by dropping them down stairs. Cranberries are often harvested by flooding the bogs so the berries float to the surface.

holidays.name: Go For A Ride Day
holidays.description: A day to get out of the house and go for a ride in a car, on a bike, on a horse, or on a motorcycle. No destination required.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance promoted in lists of fun national days, encouraging people to set aside obligations and enjoy a leisurely trip.
holidays.funFact: The word 'ride' comes from Old English 'rīdan,' which originally meant to travel on horseback. Cars and bikes came along much later.

holidays.name: Start Your Own Country Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day inviting people to declare independence, design a flag, and write an anthem for their very own micronation, even if it only covers the living room couch.
holidays.origin: A humorous unofficial observance inspired by real-life micronations, such as the Principality of Sealand, a former WWII sea fort off the coast of England that has claimed sovereignty since 1967.
holidays.funFact: Sealand has its own passports, stamps, and a royal family, though no country formally recognizes it. Its founder, Roy Bates, declared it a principality in 1967.

holidays.name: Doctor Who Anniversary Day
holidays.description: Fans around the world celebrate the birthday of the long-running British sci-fi series about a time-traveling alien and his blue police box, with marathons, scarves, and a lot of 'Wibbly wobbly, timey wimey' quotes.
holidays.origin: The first episode, 'An Unearthly Child,' aired on the BBC on November 23, 1963, but because it was broadcast on the evening after the Kennedy assassination news and in UK time, fans often start the festivities on or around November 22.
holidays.funFact: The show was almost overlooked by viewers on opening night because of the coverage of the Kennedy assassination, so the BBC reran the first episode the following week. It is now the longest-running sci-fi TV show in the world.
